function: p. 2: Joint source-channel coding of downlink CSI feedback: UE encoder sends continuous latents over noisy uplink; BS decoder plus residual-diffusion refinement reconstructs CSI, with variable compression rates.
system: p. 2, 7: FDD massive MIMO, BS with 32-antenna ULA, single-antenna UE, 32 subcarriers; uplink feedback with MRC at 5.4 GHz (QuaDRiGa); COST2100 outdoor 32x32 angular-delay CSI; no RIS.
method: p. 3-8: CNN autoencoder (supervised MSE, stage 1) plus residual-diffusion U-Net denoiser (stage 2, chi-prediction, T=20 steps, 2-step inference); Matryoshka nested latents for variable rate; Adam.
data_channel: p. 7, 10: COST2100 outdoor dataset (1e5 training, 2e4 test, 32x32 angular-delay); QuaDRiGa 3GPP TR 38.901 uplink channels at 5.4 GHz; 3GPP TR 38.901 indoor open-area dataset.
test_conditions: p. 7-11: Each model trained and tested on its own dataset split (COST2100 or 3GPP indoor), uplink SNR -10 to 10 dB; CSI-error test at CNR 0 dB.
baselines: p. 6, 12: Learned ADJSCC (small, large), deep-JSCC CSINet+ (small, large), U-Net-based JSCC, Gaussian-diffusion GD-JSCC of [37]; no classical or separate source-channel coding baseline.
metrics: p. 8-9: NMSE versus uplink SNR in angular-delay domain, uncoded BLER, encoder/decoder/diffusion throughput (samples/s), parameters and FLOPs, GPU training hours.
complexity: p. 9-10: Tables III-V: throughput (encoder 9.5e4, decoder 8.2e4, 2-step diffusion 3.9e3 samples/s on COST2100 GPU); denoiser 13.9M parameters, 271.8M FLOPs; training about 15 GPU hours.
openness: p. 1: github.com/UTAustin-ITML/rd-jscc ("Data is available on-line at"); uses the public COST2100 cropped dataset (p. 7).
q1_support: p. 7: "We evaluate our method on the COST2100 outdoor dataset [52]"; the uplink and the indoor dataset follow 3GPP TR 38.901 through QuaDRiGa (pp. 7, 10).
q2_support: p. 9: "the smaller RD-JSCC model trained on the 3GPP indoor dataset takes" 6.8 GPU hours, so each dataset has its own model tested on its own held-out split. Missing: no cross-dataset or cross-antenna test; the CNR 0 dB test (p. 11) is a CSI-error condition; k=9 to 31 are claimed on p. 6 but Fig. 6 plots only k=8, 16, 24, 32.
q3_support: p. 6: "we benchmark against ADJSCC [28], a recent state-of-the-art non-linear transform method" and CSINet+ [40], both learned. Missing: no non-learned baseline (compressed sensing or separate source and channel coding) is simulated in Sec. VI.
q4_support: p. 12: "the full RD-JSCC model has ≈ 14M parameters"; Tables IV and V (p. 10) list parameters and FLOPs per module and Table III (p. 9) the throughput.
q5_support: p. 1: "Data is available on-line at github.com/UTAustin-ITML/rd-jscc"; it also trains and tests on the public COST2100 dataset (p. 7).
notes: Area 2: CSI compression and feedback with joint source-channel coding, so the learned method performs the area 2 function. The link is multi-antenna (32 BS antennas, single-antenna UE, p. 2), so the system exclusion does not apply. q2 is 0 because the paper trains and tests inside each dataset and only varies SNR, CSI error and inference steps, which the criterion does not count. q3 is 0 because every baseline is a learned scheme or a variant of the proposed method.
